external_review._comment_alert: alert_if_missing: reserved (review is now interactive — never silently skipped)
external_review._comment_iterations: feedback_iterations: default 1 = external review is the default path. 0 = explicit opt-out; the consuming skill then runs a mandatory self-review ('2x denken') fallback instead. If > 0 and no API key is set, the skill interactively prompts the user.

models._comment: Identity-locked review models: GLM always uses its OpenRouter model; GPT uses its OpenRouter or direct model. Runtime rejects config or environment overrides that differ from these exact identifiers.

glm_routing._comment: Verified for GLM 5.3 via OpenRouter's own data-policy API (2026-09-01) AND a live production-route completion probe (plugins/shipwright-security/scripts/tools/probe_glm_zdr.py) that landed on novita. together also serves this model, though at lower measured uptime than novita. Fail closed: runtime requires this ordered declaration to match the code-owned approved endpoint registry.

deepseek_routing._comment: No longer used by the plan/code-review cascade (GLM replaced DeepSeek there, iterate-2026-09-02-glm-plan-code-review-swap) — kept for the Tier-3 PR-review gate's operator-overridable SHIPWRIGHT_PR_REVIEW_MODEL=deepseek/... path (ADR-167), which calls deepseek_openrouter_extra_body directly. Fail closed: runtime requires this ordered declaration to match the code-owned approved endpoint registry.

llm_client._comment: Timeout and retry settings for external LLM calls
llm_client._comment_timeout: Kept at 240 seconds for the shared 16000-token review budget. Keep both review clients and this shipping value in lockstep.
llm_client._comment_max_retries: Passed straight into the OpenAI() client constructor (shared/scripts/lib/external_review_degraded.py::llm_client_settings) and reused as the budget for the app-level retry-on-degraded-reply loop (retrying_completion). A former sibling field, retry_codes, was removed here (iterate-2026-09-01-external-review-retry-degradation): the OpenAI SDK's transport-level retry decides retryable status codes via a private, non-configurable _should_retry (408/409/429/>=500, which already covers this field's old [429, 500, 503] value) — there was no public API to wire a custom status-code set into, so the field only misled editors into thinking it was load-bearing.
